body:
@CaselIT has_table appears to return True for PG, SQLite.   didn't we go over all these rules for the new reflection patch in 2.0?

test case

```py
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import engine
from sqlalchemy import inspect
from sqlalchemy import text

engine = create_engine("mysql://scott:tiger@localhost/test", echo=True)
#engine = create_engine("postgresql://scott:tiger@localhost/test", echo=True)
#engine = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)

with engine.begin() as con:
    con.execute(text("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE shawn (num int)"))

    insp = inspect(con)
    assert insp.has_table("shawn")

```

this was never an intended use case for has_table() and there's not been any test support for this case, otherwise we'd have known about it.   release 1.4 has been out for two years now and it's at version 1.4.46 so I'm concerned it's a little late to make a sudden behavioral change like this.  it requires adding an additional query against innodb_temp_table_info because it's not an option to use DESCRIBE here anymore.

@CaselIT what do you think about adding has_temporary_table(), removing all temp table detection from has_table() for all dialects and doing another rc?  this really shouldn't be an accidental API Edit: OK we had some notion of coverage for this case introduced in 2.0 only, so will keep it there

rename.from: MySQL dialect has_table does not detect TEMPORARY tables anymore

body:
MariaDB actually has *no* information schema for this; their API was removed per https://jira.mariadb.org/browse/MDEV-12459.    MySQL has innodb_temp_table_info, which says nothing about other storage engines.  There's also a table_exists() function but it appears to be vapor on mariadb.

so this is so far not looking easy without reverting entirely to using DESCRIBE.

rename.to: see if mysql has_table() can support temp tables w/ DESCRIBE (again, unfortunately)

body: works fine for sqlite file, will try to re-enable

To my knowledge, MySQL’s innodb_temp_table_info doesn’t have the name of the table so you can’t use it to check for existence. DESCRIBE is the only way that I know of and I only know it as I discovered it when researching what changed in sqlalchemy that caused this bug.

I dont want this backported to 1.4 because it would be a bigger change for 1.4 than it would be for 2.0.    1.4 has been out for two years so if we knew about this use case 18 months ago, it would have been easier to revert.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**revert MySQL to use DESCRIBE for has_table()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4344

I would need to look into what test there are. I'm fairly confident this case is tested in v2 but maybe it is disabled using requirements.

Looking at the linked mariadb issue it seems that an api is still missing

That requirement was added in PS6 in this gerrit https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4160/5..6 by you mike.

Before `temp_table_names` was used for this. Maybe we could restore the behaviour?

> Before `temp_table_names` was used for this. Maybe we could restore the behaviour?

No, since mysql does not support listing temp tables

so when we did dc91c7db7ff32243cd2f6fc04f4e3a6d62f7b11b, I searched pretty hard for why we couldn't change to information_schema, the temp table use case was unknown to me at that time (though it obviously works with DESCRIBE).  We typically rely on tests failing to see if something is a regression.   then when we did db08a699489c9b0259579d7ff7fd6bf  and added has_table() tests for temp, MySQL seemed to not support it, as it also doesn't support listing temp tables, so it seemed like we should just exclude it.   The two events did not get connected (how could they).

we usually rely upon the userbase to let us know for things like this but somehow 1.4 went two years without anyone noticing.
I get the feeling that temp tables are rarely a thing
i think they are popular for SQL Server.   mysql probably not so much

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

All releases after 2.0.0rc2 appear to have the behavior described, while the releases i tested before it (2.0.0rc1, all the betas, 1.4.X, 1.3X) work fine.

```
sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (pymysql.err.OperationalError) (1049, "Unknown database 'fooschema'")
[SQL: DESCRIBE `fooschema`.`foo`]
```
You'll see the reproduction code below but essentially `event.listen(metadata, "before_create", CreateSchema("fooschema"))` appears to fail to execute the `before_create` event.

Replacing that line with `conn.execute(CreateSchema("fooschema"))` works just fine.

### To Reproduce

```python
docker run -d -e MYSQL_DATABASE=database -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=password -p 3306:3306 -it mysql:8
```

```python
from sqlalchemy import engine, MetaData, event, types, Column
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.schema import CreateSchema

metadata = MetaData()
Base = declarative_base(metadata=metadata)


class Foo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foo"
    __table_args__ = {"schema": "fooschema"}

    id = Column(types.Integer(), primary_key=True)


engine = engine.create_engine("mysql+pymysql://root:password@localhost:3306/database")
with engine.connect() as conn:
    event.listen(metadata, "before_create", CreateSchema("fooschema"))
    metadata.create_all(conn)
```
